content.alt: 33. Sharing Makes It Tastier! - My child who says "This is all mine!"
content.text:
My child who says "This is all mine!"

Whenever they get a favorite snack or toy, your child hugs it tight and shouts "It's mine!" When a friend comes near, they even turn their back sharply.

Sharing what's theirs is never an easy challenge for a child. But if you push with "Share it," the child clutches it even harder. Sharing isn't something you force — it's learned naturally when you experience the joy of it.

Curious about the sharing story? Let's explore its lesson through the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the story, too. Read the sharing story with your child and talk it over together. We've gathered many stories around 33. Sharing Makes It Tastier! — from kindness storybooks and taking-turns stories to a child who shares.

content.alt: 33. Sharing Makes It Tastier! - Sharing isn't a loss, it's double the joy
content.text:
Sharing isn't a loss, it's double the joy

It seems like having it all to yourself would make you happier, but strangely, the joy grows bigger when you share. That's because the experience of eating together and laughing together fills the heart.

A child who experiences the joy of sharing when young grows into a caring child. What matters is making sharing feel like 'a good feeling' rather than 'a rule you have to follow.'

content.alt: 33. Sharing Makes It Tastier! - The joy of sharing that Kongi discovered
content.text:
The joy of sharing that Kongi discovered

In the story Sharing Makes It Tastier!, Kongi is holding a whole armful of acorns but feels bored all alone. Then Mom says, "Yummy things taste even better when you share them."

Kongi runs to the friends and shares the acorns, saying, "I'm sorry! Let's eat together!" One for Toto, one for Bori, one for Dubu. Eating together tastes so much better, and Kongi's heart feels soft and fluffy.

content.alt: 33. Sharing Makes It Tastier! - 3 rules of sharing, learned with Tangobook
content.text:
3 rules of sharing, learned with Tangobook

The heart of this story is three rules that are easy for children to follow. One, ask your friend first! Two, share one at a time! Three, eat together!

Tangobook stories repeat these rules like a refrain, helping children naturally recall them in a moment of sharing. Through Kongi's story, they take to heart that sharing doubles both the joy and the smiles.

content.alt: 33. Sharing Makes It Tastier! - Practicing sharing together at home
content.text:
Practicing sharing together at home

After reading the book, follow up with an activity where your child hands out cookies or fruit to family and friends themselves. Rather than making them share, letting them feel the joy of sharing firsthand is the key.

And when your child shares something, point it out with "Isn't it more fun when you share?" Praising the moment of sharing generously helps your child feel proud of it and grow their sense of caring.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How do I teach my child to share?

A. Let them feel through a story that sharing makes things tastier and more fun. Rather than forcing them as if snatching something away, it's important to let them experience the joy of sharing together.

Q. Can a sharing story help?

A. Watching the story's hero grow happier by sharing with a friend nurtures your child's own wish to share. A sharing story teaches that sharing isn't a loss but a joy.

Q. My child doesn't want to share their things.

A. It's good to respect their wish to protect what's precious and not to force it. When they share on their own, praising that warmth generously opens their heart little by little.
